title: Simple Harmonic Motion (spring–mass: period, amplitude, max velocity)
theory: SHM = restoring force proportional to displacement from equilibrium: $F = -kx \Rightarrow \omega = \sqrt{k/m}$, $T = 2\pi\sqrt{m/k}$ — independent of amplitude **and of gravity**. A vertical spring merely shifts the equilibrium down by $mg/k$; the oscillation about it is unchanged. Energy: $\frac{1}{2}kA^2 = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}kx^2$ with **x measured from equilibrium**. $v_{max} = A\omega$ at equilibrium; $a_{max} = A\omega^2$ at the turning points. From an x–t graph: amplitude = peak value, period = repeat time, $v_{max} = 2\pi A/T$.
framework: Pin the amplitude from energy or a stated extreme point.
Graphs: read $A$ and $T$; never differentiate by hand.

problems.title: Maximum speed from an x–t graph

parts.parameters:
- Given: sinusoidal $x$–$t$ curve, amplitude $A$, completing one full cycle every $2t_0$ (zero crossings at $t_0$ and $2t_0$).
- Find: maximum speed.
parts.conclusion: read $T$ off the graph **first**. Trap (f) $A/t_0$ forgets the $2\pi$ of the circular-motion projection; trap (b) halves it by misreading the period.

problems.title: Ball sticks to a hanging spring–mass (parts 1–5)

parts.title: Stretch before the collision
parts.parameters:
- Given: mass $M$ hangs in equilibrium from a spring $k$; a ball $m$ moving **up** at $v$ strikes and sticks; the pair then performs SHM; gravity $g$. Extra fact for (5): at the **highest** point of the motion the spring is at its **natural length**.
- Find: initial stretch; speed just after sticking; KE lost; period; the ball's KE just before impact.
- Diagram: ceiling — spring — $M$, with $m$ rising into it from below.

parts.parameters:
- Given: mass $M$ hangs in equilibrium from a spring $k$; a ball $m$ moving **up** at $v$ strikes and sticks; the pair then performs SHM; gravity $g$. Extra fact for (5): at the **highest** point of the motion the spring is at its **natural length**.

parts.title: KE of the ball just before impact
parts.parameters:
- Given: mass $M$ hangs in equilibrium from a spring $k$; a ball $m$ moving **up** at $v$ strikes and sticks; the pair then performs SHM; gravity $g$. Extra fact for (5): at the **highest** point of the motion the spring is at its **natural length**.
- Find: initial stretch; speed just after sticking; KE lost; period; the ball's KE just before impact.
- Diagram: ceiling — spring — $M$, with $m$ rising into it from below.
parts.formulas: new equilibrium stretch $x_{eq} = \frac{(M+m)g}{k}$; at the impact instant the displacement above it is $x_1 = x_{eq} - x_0 = \frac{mg}{k}$; "natural length at the top" ⇒ amplitude $A = x_{eq} = \frac{(M+m)g}{k}$; SHM energy: $\frac{1}{2}(M+m)V^2 + \frac{1}{2}kx_1^2 = \frac{1}{2}kA^2$.
parts.conclusion: two bookkeeping facts decide everything — displacement is measured from the **new** equilibrium, and "natural length at the top" pins $A = (M+m)g/k$. Pitfall: assuming $A = mg/k$ (that is only the initial offset).

connections: 2014-Q1-(1) (Topic 8) is spring **energy without SHM**; 2018-Q1-(2) (Topic 5) is a spring in **circular** motion — don't reach for $T = 2\pi\sqrt{m/k}$ by reflex.
